title: Solving & Interpreting Differential Equations
page_title: Solving & Interpreting Differential Equations | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Maths Revision Notes 2020

blocks.text: How do I solve a differential equation from a given model?

blocks.md:
- Solving differential equations from a given model using the same techniques as before, for example separation of variables
- The precise integration method will depend on the type of question (see Decision Making)
- **Particular** **solutions** are usually required to Differential Equations ![Notes de_solve, AS & A Level Maths revision notes](assets/d596b73bec00-8-3-5-notes-de-solve.png)

  - An **initial**/**boundary** **condition** is needed
- Solutions can be rewritten in a format relevant to the model

blocks.alt: Notes de_exp_and_A, AS & A Level Maths revision notes

blocks.md:
- The solution can be used to make predictions at other times

  - Temperature after four minutes
  - Volume of sales after another three months

blocks.text: How can I use the solution of a differential equation to answer modelling questions?

blocks.md: - Questions may ask you to interpret your solutions in the context of the problem

blocks.alt: Notes de_solve_and_use_qu, AS & A Level Maths revision notes
Notes de_solve_and_use, AS & A Level Maths revision notes

blocks.md: - There could be links to other areas of A level maths – such as mechanics

- Sometimes **multiple** rates of change may be involved in a model or problem

  - See Connected Rates of Change

blocks.alt: Notes de_croc_solve1, AS & A Level Maths revision notes
Notes de_croc_solve2, AS & A Level Maths revision notes

blocks.text: How can I interpret a model using the solution to the differential equation?

blocks.md:
- Models may not always be realistic in the long term

  - A population will not grow indefinitely – it will reach a natural limit
  - You will be expected to interpret and comment on the model
